stem: Which food is traditionally from Scotland?
explanation: Haggis is a traditional Scottish dish made from sheep's stomach stuffed with offal, oats and spices. It is often eaten on Burns Night.

stem: Which dish is traditionally linked to England?
explanation: Roast beef, often served with Yorkshire pudding made from batter, is a traditional English meal.

stem: You need a TV licence to watch programmes on any device at the time they are broadcast.
explanation: A TV licence is needed to watch or record live TV on any device, including a computer or phone. The money helps pay for the BBC.

stem: What are national parks?

options.label: Protected areas of countryside that everyone can visit
Private estates that are closed to visitors

explanation: National parks are areas of protected countryside. They are open to everyone for walking, camping and other activities.

stem: What is 'Laverbread', a traditional food from Wales?
explanation: Laverbread is a traditional Welsh dish made from seaweed. It is often fried with oatmeal and served with bacon for breakfast.

stem: In England and Wales, how long can large shops open for on a Sunday?
explanation: In England and Wales, large shops (over 280 square metres) can only open for a maximum of six hours on Sundays. Small shops have no opening time limits.

stem: The National Trust is a charity that works to protect historic houses and nature.
explanation: The National Trust was founded in 1895. It has more than four million members and looks after many historic buildings and natural areas across the UK.

stem: Which TWO of the following rock bands became famous in the 1960s and 1970s?
explanation: The Rolling Stones and The Who are two of the most famous rock bands in history. They became world-famous during the 1960s and continue to be popular.

stem: Where was the popular dish 'Chicken Tikka Masala' first created?
explanation: Chicken Tikka Masala is an Indian-style dish that was actually invented in the UK. It is now considered one of the most popular meals in the country.

stem: Which BBC radio station is mostly for a younger audience and plays pop music?
explanation: BBC Radio 1 plays modern pop and rock music and is aimed at younger listeners. Radio 3 is known for classical music and Radio 4 for news and talk.

stem: The artist David Hockney is famous for which type of modern art?
explanation: David Hockney was an important part of the 1960s pop art movement. He remains one of the most influential and popular British artists of the modern era.

stem: Which of these is one of the most popular hobbies in the UK?
explanation: Gardening is a very popular hobby in the UK. Many people who do not have their own garden can rent a small piece of land called an allotment.

stem: Which TWO of the following are the largest youth organisations in the UK?
explanation: The Scout Association and Girlguiding UK are the two largest youth groups in the UK. They help young people learn new skills and participate in outdoor activities.

stem: Which artist is famous for creating works that use animals preserved in chemicals?
explanation: Damien Hirst is a leading member of the 'Young British Artists' group. He is famous for work that includes animals preserved in liquid.

stem: On which day of the week do many shops in town centres stay open late?
explanation: Many shops in town centres stay open later than usual on Thursday evenings. This is often called 'late-night shopping'.

stem: Volunteering is when people work for no pay to help their local community.
explanation: Volunteering is a great way to help the community and meet new people. Many charities and groups in the UK rely on volunteers to do their work.

stem: What name is given to large cinemas that have many screens showing different films?
explanation: Most towns and cities in the UK have a large cinema called a multiplex. These buildings have several screens showing many different films at the same time.

stem: In which part of London is the National Gallery located?
explanation: The National Gallery is a famous art museum in Trafalgar Square, London. It houses a collection of more than 2,000 Western European paintings.

stem: Which city hosts the largest arts festival in the world every summer?
explanation: The Edinburgh Festival is held every August in Scotland's capital. It is the largest arts festival in the world and includes many theatre and comedy shows.

stem: Which part of England is famous for the 'Cornish Pasty', which is a pastry filled with meat and vegetables?
explanation: The Cornish Pasty comes from Cornwall in the South West of England. It was originally made as a portable meal for miners to take to work.

stem: Which area in London is world-famous for its many theatres and musical shows?
explanation: The West End is the centre of the theatre industry in London. Many world-famous musicals and plays have been running there for decades.

stem: Which TWO of the following are examples of traditional British desserts or puddings?
explanation: Apple crumble and bread and butter pudding are classic British desserts. They are often served with custard, which is a sweet, yellow sauce.

stem: Many people in the UK rent a small piece of land called an 'allotment' to grow their own fruit and vegetables.
explanation: Allotments are popular with people who do not have a garden at home. They are a great way to spend time outdoors and grow fresh food.

stem: Which of these is a traditional British meal of tea, sandwiches, and small cakes often served in the late afternoon?
explanation: Afternoon tea is a famous British tradition. It usually includes scones with jam and cream, along with a selection of finger sandwiches.

stem: Which of these is a famous type of cheese that was first made in a village in Somerset, England?
explanation: Cheddar is the most popular type of cheese in the UK. It was originally made in the village of Cheddar in the county of Somerset.
